Assistant Professor of Physics - Theoretical Atomic, Molecular, and Optical Physics


University of Oklahoma, Norman Campus





The Homer L. Dodge Department of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Oklahoma (OU) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in theoretical Atomic, Molecular, and Optical (AMO) physics with a starting date of August 16, 2027. This position in fundamental research is associated with the Center for Quantum Research and Technology (CQRT) at OU. The CQRT (https://ou.edu/cqrt) is hosted in a state-of-the-art physics building with 18,000 square feet of laboratory space that meets NIST-A specifications on environmental control. Campus resources include supercomputer access.





Successful candidates are expected to teach effectively at both the undergraduate and graduate levels (one class per semester), maintain an outstanding record of original published research, and develop an internationally recognized, externally funded research program that complements and expands existing research efforts at OU.

• Ph.D. in physics or a closely related field and post Ph.D. experience.

• Demonstrated record of research accomplishments in theoretical AMO physics or closely related field.






Preferred Qualifications:



• Demonstrated evidence to teach effectively and to effectively mentor students.






Applicants must apply for this position online at the quick link https://apply.interfolio.com/192488

Cover letter (3 pages max). The letter may address examples of the candidate’s approach to teaching, research, service, mentorship, outreach, etc.



• Curriculum vitae.

• Description of past research and future research plans (3-5 pages), demonstrating potential to attract external funding.

• Description of past teaching and/or future plans (2 pages max).

The search committee will begin reviewing applications on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled.





Inquiries should be directed to the search committee chair:


Professor Doerte Blume - doerte.blume-1@ou.edu

jobs.title: Research Assistant Professor - Computational Biology or Systems Immunology
jobs.description:
CAREERS AT OKLAHOMA MEDICAL RESEARCH FOUNDATION

Have big ideas, passion, and a desire to grow? Join us and make a difference.

For multiple consecutive years, Foundation employees have voted OMRF among “Oklahoma’s Top Workplaces.”

Our mission: "...so that more may live longer, healthier lives." Learn more .
Research Assistant Professor - Computational Biology or Systems Immunology

Position Overview and Responsibilities
The James/Guthridge Lab (james.omrf.org ; guthridge.omrf.org ) is hiring a Research Assistant Professor (transitional faculty member) to assist with analysis of large, complex, multi-modal datasets from clinical trials and clinical research protocols. The successful candidate will have training and expertise in computational biology, systems immunology, bioinformatics, biostatistics, machine learning, or related quantitative disciplines to add to one of the nation's leading multidisciplinary autoimmune disease research programs, OMRF Arthritis & Clinical Immunology .

This position offers an exceptional opportunity to become part of a highly collaborative team of physician-scientists, immunologists, computational biologists, geneticists, epidemiologists, and data scientists dedicated to understanding the mechanisms underlying autoimmune diseases and developing strategies to predict, prevent, and treat them.

The successful candidate will leverage large, deeply phenotyped, multi-modal datasets generated from patients with autoimmune diseases and individuals at risk for developing autoimmunity. Available data include high-dimensional molecular, cellular, genetic, genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, clinical, imaging, and longitudinal biospecimen datasets derived from peripheral blood and disease-relevant tissues. These resources provide outstanding opportunities for integrative analyses, biomarker discovery, mechanistic investigation, disease prediction, and precision medicine.

This is a transitional position for scientists who have completed a graduate degree and an exemplary postdoctoral experience who have been evaluated as being likely to develop high-caliber independent or collaborative projects and to attract extramural grant support. Successful candidates are characterized by considerable experience, highly distinctive competence, and a demonstrated ability to perform both independently and as a critical member of a large multi-disciplinary productive team.
Minimum Qualifications
• Ph.D. in a biological science, chemistry, physics or other relevant area such as statistics, biostatistics, applied mathematics, epidemiology, and/or M.D., or equivalent and typically two or more years of exemplary postdoctoral experience.
• Must be a team-player with good organizational and communication skills.
• Must be able to work independently, as well as highly attentive to detail, and dependable.
• Must be interested in contributing to the preparation and development of federal and foundation grant applications.

Preferred Qualifications
• The ability to perform data analysis and visualization using appropriate analytic software programs or through programming in R, Python or other languages.
• Human Immune response in heath and disease experience or clinical trials experience strongly preferred.
• At least 5 publications, including publications in high-impact journals.
• Experience writing parts of successful grant applications.

OMRF Overview
Founded in 1946, the Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation (OMRF) is among the nation’s oldest, most respected independent, nonprofit biomedical research institutes. jobs.title: Data Product Analyst
jobs.description:
Koch Engineered Solutions is seeking a Data Product Analyst for the ET&S data delivery team. The role sits at the intersection of governance, data quality, and product delivery. It translates governance standards into actionable insights that help data stewards and data owners improve and manage their data domains. It keeps the reporting on our data products clear, current, and trusted. It is an ideal first role for someone who is analytical, organized, and eager to learn how a modern data organization runs.

Working closely with internal customers, Data Engineers (DE), and Data Analysts (DA), this role helps prioritize and communicate data product work, develop data-quality scorecards, support governance reporting, and maintain visibility into team priorities and progress. Success in the role is measured by the clarity of the insights produced and the reliability of the reporting and coordination the individual provides. This position is based in our Tulsa, OK or Wichita, KS offices. This position is not eligible for Visa Sponsorship.

Our Team

The Data & Information Technology team is collaboratively focused on transforming business data into trusted, actionable information that enables effective decision making across Koch Engineered Solutions. Our team brings together data analysts, business data specialists, and data governance to partner closely with stakeholders to improve data quality, streamline decision making, and support digital transformation initiatives. We thrive on solving complex business challenges, driving continuous improvement, and creating practical solutions that help our organization work smarter. Above all, we value teamwork, curiosity, and a commitment to delivering reliable data that drives long-term business value.

What You Will Do

• Translate enterprise data governance standards and policies into clear, analyst-ready requirements.

• Support governance metrics and the insight needs of data owners, helping them monitor and steward their data domains.

• Pair with data engineers (DE) and data analysts (DA) to build and refine KPI reporting on the team's data products.

• Maintain visibility into data product priorities, progress, and dependencies, ensuring stakeholders have clear insight into status, risks, and upcoming work.

• Partner with stakeholders to evaluate, document, and prioritize new governance, reporting, and data quality opportunities.

• Document data definitions, quality rules, and reporting logic so governance artifacts stay accurate and reusable.

• Facilitate routine reviews of scorecards and KPIs, flagging trends, gaps, and data-quality issues for follow-up.

• Partner with stakeholders to communicate changes to data definitions, quality rules, and governance standards, helping ensure successful implementation

• Monitor data product usage and adoption metrics, identifying opportunities to improve value delivery and support retirement decisions when products no longer meet business needs.

Who You Are (Basic Qualifications)

• Experience working with data in tools such as Excel or Power BI and foundational SQL skills.

• Experience translating technical details into plain-language requirements and status updates.

• Experience collaborating effectively across both technical and non-technical business teams.

• Understanding principles, concepts, and terminology used in a data organization.

What Will Put You Ahead

• Bachelor's degree in a related field (data analytics, information systems, business, or statistics) .

• Exposure to data governance concepts such as data ownership, stewardship, quality dimensions, and metadata.

• Experience with backlog or work-tracking tools (for example, Azure DevOps or Jira) and agile ways of working.

• Exposure to prompt engineering and refinement.

• Familiar with ETO/manufacturing organizations.

• Experience leveraging generative AI to streamline workflows and improve outcomes.

    • Support data integration with third-party systems to enhance reporting capabilities
  • Data Quality Control:
    • Partner with engineers to validate data accuracy, integrity, and consistency
    • Implement data validation processes to maintain high-quality analytical outputs
  • Perform Advanced Analytics
    • Conduct deep analysis of workforce and productivity trends using SQL and Python
    • Deliver data-driven recommendations that empower customers to optimize performance and decision-making
  • Facilitate Internal Ad-hoc Data Requests:
    • Support cross-functional teams (HR, Operations, Product) by querying key datasets from Google BigQuery
    • Ensure timely and accurate responses to ad-hoc data needs
  • Enhance Productivity Metrics:
    • Collaborate on the development and refinement of productivity measurement frameworks
    • Align metrics with evolving business goals and customer needs

Requirements

Skills & Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field such as Data Analytics, Business Analytics, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Computer Science, or a related discipline
  • Minimum 3 years of experience in:
    • SQL (advanced queries and optimization)
    • BI tools (Tableau, Power BI w/ DAX & PowerQuery, Looker Studio, or Qlik)
    • Python
    • API Integrations
    • Data analysis, metrics development, and cross-functional reporting
    • ETL and Data Warehousing
    • AppScripts & PowerShell
  • Hands-on experience with Google BigQuery and Google Cloud Platform
  • Strong storytelling and communication skills to influence stakeholders at all levels
  • Self-starter with a growth mindset and attention to detail
  • Excellent communication skills with both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Ability to deal with ambiguity and collaborate with different teams towards mutual goals
  • Motivated by an interest in developing the best possible solutions

Preferred

  • Experience in Workforce Analytics

Benefits

Work environment

  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Position is remote within US
  • Minimal travel
  • Limited physical demands

jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The Scientific Programmer I - Algorithm Integration supports the integration, testing, and operational readiness of scientific algorithms and software products in a remote work environment. This role documents algorithm workflows, establishes testing processes, validates outputs, troubleshoots issues, and ensures reliable delivery of production-ready solutions.

Success in this role is demonstrated through accurate algorithm implementation, effective collaboration with Science Teams and stakeholders, and the successful transition of validated software into operational environments.

What You Will Do in This Role

The Scientific Programmer II - Algorithm Integration supports the operationalization of scientific algorithms by documenting requirements, integrating and validating code, establishing testing processes, ensuring output accuracy, and collaborating with scientific and technical stakeholders to deliver reliable production-ready solutions.
• Analyze and document algorithm inputs, outputs, workflows, and production rules across operational units, identifying variations in requirements and implementation approaches.
• Define and maintain operational execution procedures, including run triggers, intermediate data exchanges, processing workflows, and final delivered output products.
• Establish, maintain, and validate project baseline test cases in collaboration with Science Teams to support consistent software verification.
• Evaluate code updates and enhancements against established baselines to identify impacts, maintain functionality, and support regression testing activities.
• Review and analyze regression test results to identify issues, verify fixes, and ensure continued algorithm reliability.
• Coordinate with Science Teams and technical stakeholders to communicate progress, resolve issues, manage dependencies, and track project activities through tools such as Jira.
• Integrate and validate software components in alignment with coding standards, interface requirements, build processes, and project documentation checklists.
• Verify output products for accuracy, quality, format compliance, logging requirements, and adherence to operational standards.
• Troubleshoot, optimize, and debug code while supporting updates to input/output file formats and data processing workflows.
• Develop and maintain technical documentation, including production rules, delivery documentation, operational procedures, and user guidance materials.
• Demonstrate delivered software capabilities and production workflows while providing technical support during transition to operational environments.
• Develop and execute test cases to evaluate impacts from upstream data changes and support downstream algorithm enhancements.

What You Will Bring
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, or a related scientific or technical discipline.
• 2-4 years of experience in system integration, software deployment, or IT operations.
• Hands-on experience with one or more of the following programming languages: FORTRAN, C, or C++, supporting application development, integration, maintenance, or performance-focused initiatives.
• Working knowledge of Python for application support, scripting, or automation.
• Strong understanding of configuration management, APIs, system interfaces, and data flow between interconnected systems.
• Experience with container technologies, preferably Docker, and container orchestration platforms such as Kubernetes.
• Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot, analyze, and resolve complex software integration issues.
• Strong documentation, communication, and coordination skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across technical teams.

OWL Services is the premier sales, installation, program management and service provider to retail, commercial, fleet, aviation and marine, and emergency power generation companies across the U.S.

Come join us! For more information visit OWLServices.com and follow us on LinkedIn .

We are looking for a Data Analyst to join our Data Warehouse & BI team and help us expand the reach, depth, and operational impact of our modern data platform. This is a hands-on role focused on report development, model expansion, and the ongoing reliability of a production analytics stack that already drives company-wide reporting.

jobs.description:
University of Oklahoma Norman Campus:
Dodge Family College of Arts and Sciences:
Physics and Astronomy Location

Norman, OK
Open Date

Apr 06, 2026
Description

Available immediately. Experimental postdoc position in atomic physics pursuing implementations of quantum information science (QIS) in neutral atom systems within the contexts of quantum sensing with atom interferometers, and/or multi-atom entanglement using interactions between ultra-cold Rydberg atoms in optical tweezers. These research directions build upon our prior, foundational work with entangling interactions using ultra-cold Rydberg atoms controlled in optical tweezers, as well as novel techniques for matter wave interferometry.

Our current investigations cover aspects of matter wave interferometry, quantum synchronization, and an exploration of computational complexity versus robustness with entangled atomic spins. Main duties include leading, developing, and managing QIS experiments that advance these research directions. The initial appointment is for two years, with the possibility of renewal for a third year, contingent on satisfactory performance and continued funding.

The stipend will be $65,000 per year plus benefits along with an annual $4,000 travel budget for the Fellow.
Qualifications

Applicants must have a Ph.D. in Physics or a related area.
Application Instructions

Applicants should submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae (including publications), a statement of research interests and plans limited to two pages to interfolio. Applicants will be asked to provide contact information of three confidential letter writers, who will be subsequently contacted. Applicants are asked to indicate their potential start date in the cover letter.

This institution is using Interfolio's Faculty Search to conduct this search. Applicants to this position receive a free Dossier account and can send all application materials, including confidential letters of recommendation, free of charge.
